title: Two ways of ranking national teams agree moderately
headline_insight: Ranking 153 shared national teams by trailing-10 form win-rate versus net-xG strength gives a Spearman rho of 0.6419 -- moderate agreement between two independent lenses, not a temporal persistence test.
what_it_means: This is a parallel-forms check: a recent-form ranking and a full-history strength ranking land in broadly the same order (Pearson r 0.6369 alongside the rho 0.6419). Read it as convergent validity -- the two measures see the same underlying quality -- rather than as proof that form persists over time.
how_to_read: Each point is a national team plotted by its trailing-10 form win-rate against its net-xG strength score; a tighter, more monotonic scatter is a higher rank correlation.
why_it_matters: The intended stronger test -- a temporal split-half (first-half vs second-half of a season) -- cannot be built here: the claim store holds only one as-of ranking vector per metric, with no within-season time series to cut into halves.
caveat: DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY, edge_claimed false; NOT a temporal split-half and NOT a predictor (soccer_intl's predictive gate is CLOSED upstream). Form win-rate is quantized to one decimal (tie_fraction_form 0.9346), which inflates ties and pulls the correlation toward zero.
